items_missed: 1_set_agenda: No full agenda statement up front (what she'd cover + rough time) and no explicit 'sound good?' confirmation — she only asked 'is this a good time?', which is a different ask.

2_probe: Never asked about additional rooms/garage/storage unit, never asked about a storage stop, and never asked the open 'anything you're particularly worried about with this move?' stressor question.
3_pricing: Skipped the 'pricing is super simple' opener, and never mentioned Meet Your Mover or the On-Time Guarantee anywhere in the call.
4_clock: Never framed the clock as starting on-site when the contract opens.

6_save_your_ass: No real prep speech — no consolidation examples (kids' toys, garden tools, drawers, wall photos), no explicit 'take a carload' tip, and no 'does that make sense?' close on this topic. The 'stage boxes near the door' line is close but doesn't reach the bar.

7_quote_booking: Never attempted to lock in a booking on the call itself, didn't mention a bolded detail list at the top of the confirmation email, and never stated business hours or how to reach the branch.
8_politeness: Only addressed the customer by name twice in the whole call (as 'Selena' — very likely an ASR mangling of Celina, the name in the header) — short of the 3+ threshold.

9_bonus: No 60-cents-per-pound baseline comparison alongside the No Worries damage coverage, and no response to the customer's direct 'I'm getting other quotes' comment with any value or budget framing.
top_strength: Genuine patience when the customer got flustered finding her new address mid-call at Costco — 'Take your time, no worries, take your time' — kept the call calm instead of rushing her, and the pricing breakdown (truck, blankets, wrap, tools, taxes, insurance, gas, no fees) was delivered fully and clearly without being prompted.
coaching_note: You're patient and easy to listen to, and your pricing walkthrough was thorough. But you're leaving the close on the table: Celina told you flat out she's comparing other quotes, and you answered with 'no worries' instead of making the value case (No Worries coverage, no deposit, no hidden fees) or asking directly if she wants to lock in one of the two open slots today. Build out the actual Save Your Ass speech — you hinted at 'stage boxes near the door' but never gave a real consolidation example or the carload tip — and work in Meet Your Mover and the On-Time Guarantee so she has every differentiator before she compares you to competitors.
phone_presence_notes: Consistently warm and reassuring under a distracted, fumbling customer, and the customer explicitly said 'you've been so helpful' at the close, though the call stayed short of standout rapport-building (no humor, no strong emotional acknowledgment of her price-shopping hesitation).
